title: Jasper Complex Wildfire Burn Scar 2024
headline: Intense wildfire destroyed over 330 km² of montane pine forest canopy in Athabasca Valley.
story: In late July 2024, lightning ignitions combined with prolonged drought sparked the Jasper Complex Wildfire. Driven by 100 km/h winds and wall-of-fire crown blazes, the fire swept through the Athabasca River valley and into the historic townsite of Jasper. Dense pyrocumulonimbus smoke plumes choked optical instruments, while radar microwave sensors mapped canopy burn severity in real time.
why_sar: Why radar sees through cloud and night: Dense pyrocumulonimbus smoke clouds reaching the stratosphere completely blinded visible sensors; radar waves penetrated directly through the dense smoke canopy.
